diff-tour.name: diff-tour (init-co-jp/diff-tour, Go terminal app that has an LLM write a guided tour of a git diff)

questions.q: Trace what happens inside ky when a GET request gets a 503 response and retries are enabled. Name the internal methods involved, in order, and say when the beforeRetry hooks run.
points: The request goes run -> retry -> fetch (the private #run, #retry and #fetch methods, or equivalent names)
afterResponse hooks run on the 503 response before ky decides to throw or retry
A HTTPError is created and the retry decision (#retryFromError / #calculateRetryDelay) checks the retry limit, the method and the status code list
The delay comes from the Retry-After style header for statuses in afterStatusCodes (capped by maxRetryAfter), otherwise from retry.delay (0.3 s doubling) with optional jitter, capped by backoffLimit
ky waits for the delay first; beforeRetry hooks run after the delay and before the next fetch, then the retry count goes up and fetch runs again

questions.q: How does ky enforce the `timeout` option on a single attempt, and what happens to the timeout when the request is retried?
points: A timeout() helper races fetch against a setTimeout timer
When the timer fires it aborts ky's AbortController and rejects with a TimeoutError
Each attempt gets its own timeout (the timer is cleared in finally), limited by the remaining totalTimeout budget when one is set
TimeoutError is only retried when retryOnTimeout is enabled (or shouldRetry returns true); by default it is not
Before a retry after a timeout, the aborted AbortController is replaced with a fresh one (new managed signal) so the next attempt is not born aborted

questions.q: In what order do ky's hooks run during one request that keeps failing with an HTTP error until the retries run out, and which hooks can replace the response?
points: init hooks run first, synchronously, on the options before the request is built
beforeRequest hooks run once before the first fetch; returning a Response skips the fetch (and that response is not retried)
afterResponse hooks run after every response, including each retry; they can return a new Response or force a retry with ky.retry()
beforeRetry hooks run before each retry attempt; they can return a Request, a Response, or ky.stop
beforeError hooks run last, once, when the final HTTPError is thrown; they can return a modified error

questions.q: When I call `ky.get(url).json()`, how does the Accept header get set to application/json even though `.json()` is called after `ky.get()` already returned?
points: Ky.create returns a promise object with body method shortcuts (json, text, blob...) attached
The shortcut sets the accept header to the method's MIME type on the pending request, unless an Accept header is already set
The fetch is delayed by one microtask (#run starts with await Promise.resolve()) so the synchronous shortcut call runs before the request is sent
If the request was already sent, the header only changes later attempts (the shortcut checks request vs original request)
The json shortcut then reads the body as text and parses it with parseJson or JSON.parse (with optional schema validation)

questions.q: How can an afterResponse hook force ky to retry a request, and how does a forced retry differ from a normal retry?
points: The hook returns ky.retry(...), which ky turns into a ForceRetryError
The run loop catches the ForceRetryError from the afterResponse hooks and goes to the retry path even for a successful response
A forced retry skips the retriable-method check, shouldRetry and the status code list
It still counts against the retry limit, and can carry a custom delay (used instead of the computed backoff)
It can carry a custom Request, which is applied before the beforeRetry hooks run

questions.q: Trace a call to `requests.get(url)` down to the network: which functions and classes run, in order?
points: requests.get calls api.request, which opens a Session in a with block and calls session.request
Session.request builds a Request and calls prepare_request (merging session headers, cookies, auth and hooks into a PreparedRequest)
Session.request calls merge_environment_settings (proxies, verify, cert from the environment) and then Session.send
Session.send picks an adapter with get_adapter and calls HTTPAdapter.send, which uses a urllib3 connection pool (urlopen) and build_response
After the adapter, send dispatches the response hooks, extracts cookies into the session jar and follows redirects with resolve_redirects

questions.q: How does a requests Session follow redirects, and when does it drop the Authorization header on a redirect?
points: Session.send calls resolve_redirects, a generator, when allow_redirects is true
Each hop reads the Location header (get_redirect_target), consumes and closes the old response, and stops with TooManyRedirects at max_redirects (30)
rebuild_method changes the method (303 and 302 to GET unless HEAD, 301 only for POST)
rebuild_auth removes the Authorization header when should_strip_auth is true, which happens when the hostname changes
An http to https upgrade on the same host with default ports keeps the header; other scheme or port changes strip it

questions.q: How does requests pick which transport adapter handles a URL, and how do you plug in your own adapter?
points: A new Session mounts an HTTPAdapter for both https:// and http://
get_adapter loops over the mounted adapters and returns the first whose prefix matches the start of the URL, case-insensitively
mount keeps the adapters ordered by prefix length, longest first, so the most specific prefix wins
If no prefix matches, get_adapter raises InvalidSchema
To plug in your own: subclass BaseAdapter (or HTTPAdapter), implement send and close, and call session.mount(prefix, adapter)

questions.q: Where do proxy and CA bundle settings from environment variables get merged into a requests call, and which source wins when they conflict?
points: Session.request calls merge_environment_settings after preparing the request, and it only reads the environment when trust_env is true
Environment proxies come from get_environ_proxies (respecting no_proxy) and are added with setdefault, so proxies passed explicitly win
REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, then CURL_CA_BUNDLE, replace verify when verify is True or None
Then merge_setting combines request-level and session-level values, with the request-level value winning
Consequence: session.verify = False can be overridden by a CA bundle from the environment, because the request-level verify is None and gets the env value first

questions.q: In requests, what happens to cookies set by a response, and how do response hooks run?
points: Session.send calls dispatch_hook('response', hooks, r) right after the adapter returns
dispatch_hook calls each hook in turn, and a hook that returns a value replaces the response passed on
Session hooks and request hooks are merged in prepare_request (merge_hooks)
After the hooks, extract_cookies_to_jar stores the response cookies in the session's cookie jar (also for responses in history)
During redirects, cookies are extracted again and the next request's Cookie header is rebuilt from the jar

questions.q: Trace what happens from running `tour feature/x` until the tour appears on screen: which functions run, in order?
points: main.run parses flags, loads the config and resolve() turns a branch name into base = the default branch and head = the branch
ui.NewGenerating / App.start computes a CacheKey and opens the saved tour with LoadCached if there is one
Otherwise generate.Generate runs in a goroutine: PrepareWorkspace exports the merge base and head with git archive into base/ and head/ plus change.diff and commits.txt, and writes the lessons
buildPrompt assembles the prompt and backend.Run runs the LLM CLI (for Claude Code, claude -p with stream-json) in that workspace
The reply is parsed and validated (settle, with up to 2 repair rounds), saved with SaveCached, and openViewer shows it

questions.q: What does diff-tour do when the LLM's reply is not a valid tour?
points: extractJSON cuts the reply at a separator line and takes the text from the first { to the last }
If the reply has no JSON at all, the generation is run once more instead of asking for a fix
parse decodes with unknown fields disallowed, runs Validate, and render.Check verifies that referenced files, line ranges and hunks exist
The problems are sent back in a repair prompt, with the previous JSON written to draft.txt in the workspace
At most MaxRepairs = 2 repair rounds, then it fails with InvalidTourError listing the problems

questions.q: How does diff-tour keep the LLM from changing the user's repository or reading files outside it?
points: The LLM works in an exported copy (a workspace in the cache directory made with git archive), not in the repository
Extraction skips absolute paths and paths that climb out with .., and does not export symlinks
For Claude Code it passes --restricted and --tools Read,Grep,Glob (read-only tools only)
It also passes --permission-mode dontAsk and --strict-mcp-config (no MCP servers, no prompts)
The workspace is deleted when generation finishes

questions.q: When does diff-tour reuse a saved tour instead of asking the LLM again, and what makes it regenerate?
points: CacheKey is a sha256 over the merge base, the head commit, the language, PromptVersion and the backend name (first 24 hex chars)
Saved tours live in the user cache directory under tour/tours/<key>.json
App.start loads the saved tour with LoadCached and opens it without calling the LLM
A new commit on the branch, a different language or LLM, or a bumped PromptVersion gives a new key and a new tour
The branch picker shows which targets are already cached, and answers to reader questions are saved back into the cached tour

questions.q: How does asking a question during a tour work in diff-tour, from typing the question to the new steps appearing?
points: The viewer opens an ask panel (with suggested questions) and startAnswer runs generate.Answer in the background
Answer prepares the same workspace as a tour and also writes the whole tour as tour.json
askPrompt lists the tour steps with the current one marked, includes the current step's JSON and the reader's question
The reply goes through the same parse and repair loop (settle) and its steps are taken out of the returned chapters
The new steps are inserted right after the current step (InsertAfter), marked with the question, and saved to the cached tour when possible
